solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spoilt socialite girl once set about keeping delicate

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so the turned-round girl goes around the next piece
set about means turned around, so the debutante is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, was a young society woman making her entrance in the old days
delicate as in a light touch or light meal

explanation.surface: A pampered society girl of yesteryear sets about protecting something fragile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' means turned round, and 'keeping' means holding; a deb was a debutante, a girl presented to high society.
explanation.definitionFit: Blighted crops or hopes are ruined, a direct synonym of spoilt.

clue.text: University accommodation set up in most superior capital

indicators.note: in places the university and lodgings pieces inside the other word

parts.note: the most superior is the best

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means written upwards, so this word reads backwards

parts.note: a pad is slang for a flat or lodgings

explanation.surface: Student lodgings are built inside the finest city.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'set up' means read from the bottom; 'in' wraps the university and lodgings pieces inside the word for most superior.
explanation.definitionFit: Budapest is the capital city of Hungary, so it is an example of a capital.

clue.text: Conclude there's no escaping from hell

indicators.note: escaping from says the word no gets out of the word for hell and leaves it

parts.note: the inferno is a name for hell, as in Dante

explanation.surface: A grim reflection that once damned there is no way out of hell.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to reason towards a conclusion, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Is the boss giving warning in America?

definitions.meaning: to head up a team or department is to lead it, to be in charge
an American interjection telling people to look out for something coming

explanation.surface: Is the manager the one shouting a warning across the Atlantic?
explanation.definitionFit: Heads-up is US slang for an alert, and heads up as a verb phrase means leads or runs something.

clue.text: Row, missing edges in lake

indicators.note: missing edges says the first and last letters of the word for a row are dropped

parts.note: a row of things is a series

explanation.surface: A rowing boat without its sides out on a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America, so it is an example of a lake.

clue.text: Fighting that brings lawsuit

definitions.meaning: ... is military combat, as in killed in ...
a legal ... is a case brought in court

explanation.surface: Combat that ends in a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: Action means both battle and a legal proceeding, two separate dictionary senses of one noun.

clue.text: Mark Liverpudlian songstress enthralling journalist

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the singer's name wraps around the journalist

parts.note: Cilla Black was a pop singer and TV presenter from Liverpool
ED is short for editor, the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A Liverpool singer captivating a reporter becomes a mark of note.
explanation.walkthrough: Cilla Black was a 1960s Liverpool singer, later a British TV host.
explanation.definitionFit: A cedilla is the hook-shaped diacritical mark under a letter, as in the French word garçon.

clue.text: Educated girl being restricted, awfully tired and angry

indicators.note: being restricted says the girl is hemmed in by the scrambled letters around her
awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters of tired are mixed up

parts.note: a reference to the play and film Educating Rita, whose heroine is educated by a tutor

explanation.surface: A schooled young woman, hemmed in and exhausted, is fuming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' scrambles the word tired around the girl; 'being restricted' says she is boxed in by those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritated means annoyed or cross, a mild synonym of angry.

clue.text: End of match? Numbers go into 'iding

parts.note: to go into hiding is to hide; with the dropped H shown by the apostrophe it becomes ide

explanation.surface: A Cockney talks of numbers going into hiding at full time.
explanation.walkthrough: No-side is the referee's call ending a rugby match. The apostrophe in 'iding tells the solver to drop the H of HIDE too.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby the call of no-side marks the final whistle, the close of play.

clue.text: Admit fees may be ridiculous, giving up too easily?

indicators.note: may be ridiculous suggests something absurdly jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Admitting the charges are absurd is simply throwing in the towel.
explanation.definitionFit: Defeatism is the attitude of expecting failure and surrendering readily, which the question-marked phrase describes.

clue.text: After a while thief gets alias

indicators.note: After says the thief piece follows the piece for a while

parts.note: MO, short for moment, means a short while
a nicker is someone who nicks, British slang for steals

explanation.surface: A burglar eventually takes on a false name.
explanation.walkthrough: To nick is British slang for to steal, so a nicker is a thief.
explanation.definitionFit: A moniker is a name or nickname, so alias is a close synonym.

clue.text: Game in which valuable instrument gets knocked over

indicators.note: knocked over suggests something turned upside down, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: a Strad is a Stradivarius violin, famously valuable

explanation.surface: A pub game in which a priceless violin is accidentally sent flying.
explanation.definitionFit: Darts is a pub game played by throwing small arrows at a board.

clue.text: Fairies, with the first sign of hunger, pass away

parts.note: peris are fairies or elves in Persian mythology

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Fairy folk, starting to go hungry, waste away.
explanation.walkthrough: PERI is a Persian fairy, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To perish is to die, so pass away is a gentle synonym.

clue.text: Puffed up? One man's the opposite of that inside

parts.note: inside gives IN
the opposite of being puffed up is being flat
Ed is one man, by his short name

explanation.surface: Is a swollen thing simply the reverse of a deflated one?
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as 'Ed is inside the flat': 'the opposite of that' points back to 'Puffed up', whose opposite is flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inflated has been blown up with air, so it is puffed up.

clue.text: What's to get stirred up about, being moved from slums?

indicators.note: about here means around, so the word for stirred up goes around the other piece

parts.note: to be roused is to be stirred up or excited
eh is a questioning what, as in eh?

explanation.surface: What is there to be agitated about in slum clearance?
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' means surrounding: the word for stirred up surrounds a questioning 'what?'.
explanation.definitionFit: People given new homes when slums are cleared are rehoused, moved to better accommodation.

clue.text: Tramp's chancer on the move — he recycles useful stuff

indicators.note: on the move suggests letters shifting about, so these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vagrant chancer roams about, collecting things others might use.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'Tramp's' counts as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap merchant buys and sells discarded metal and goods so they can be reused.

clue.text: Denying what ram may be doing again!

parts.note: RE as a prefix means again
rams butt with their horns

explanation.surface: A ram charging once more, its head down.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebutting a claim means contradicting or refuting it, so it is a synonym of denying.

clue.text: Release worker providing blank cheque

parts.note: to release is to free
a hand is a manual worker, as in a farm hand

explanation.surface: Setting a labourer loose gives him unlimited spending power.
explanation.definitionFit: A free hand is complete freedom to act as one likes, which a blank cheque figuratively grants.

clue.text: One detects a lot of different lines in the supermarket

definitions.text: One detects a lot of different lines in the supermarket

parts.words: One detects a lot of different lines in the supermarket
parts.note: reads like a shopper spotting product ranges, but the lines are the stripes on goods read at the checkout

explanation.surface: A shopper noticing many product ranges in the store.
explanation.definitionFit: This scanner reads the striped codes printed on goods, so it detects many lines of differing thickness at the till.

clue.text: Lock of hair enclosed by adoring letter-writer

indicators.note: enclosed by says the answer sits within the following run of letters

explanation.surface: A lover sends a lock of hair in a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a long curled lock of hair.

clue.text: Listener subsequently like a crock?

parts.note: the ear is the organ that listens
subsequently means afterwards, then

explanation.surface: A listener later likened to an old wreck.
explanation.walkthrough: Crock looks like the slang for a broken-down person, but here it is a clay pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A crock is a clay pot, so earthenware vessels are earthen, made of baked clay.

clue.text: European male getting round capital of Malta in cab

parts.note: Hans is a common German man's name
O is round in shape

indicators.note: capital of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A German fellow travelling around Malta's capital by taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: A hansom is a two-wheeled horse-drawn cab of the Victorian era.

clue.text: Surprise in wood — great weight is buried

indicators.note: buried says the following pieces lie inside the word for wood

parts.note: ash is a kind of tree and its timber
a ton is a large unit of weight

explanation.surface: A surprise in the forest: something very heavy lies buried.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish is to amaze, a strong synonym of surprise used as a verb.

clue.text: Very big drink that's rubbish, litre swallowed

indicators.note: swallowed says the litre piece goes inside the word for rubbish

parts.note: tripe is nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A huge, terrible drink, a whole litre downed.
explanation.definitionFit: A triple is a treble measure of spirits, a very large drink.

clue.text: The two characters making pa a beast

definitions.text: The two characters making pa a beast

parts.words: The two characters making pa a beast
parts.note: the two letters of pa, spelt out with the word and between them, name an animal

explanation.surface: Two letters make Dad an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: Write out the two letters of 'pa' as you would say them, joined by 'and', and an animal appears.
explanation.definitionFit: The black-and-white bear of China is spelt by naming pa's two letters joined together.

clue.text: It's almost total laziness in niche of organisation

indicators.note: almost says the word for laziness is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: sloth is utter idleness

explanation.surface: Idleness nearly takes over a corner of the company.
explanation.definitionFit: A slot is a place or position in a schedule or structure, a niche within an organisation.

clue.text: Person deemed to be good — and bad, for all that

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated ST, is a person thought holy
ill means bad, as in ill will

explanation.surface: Someone believed virtuous may still be wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Still as an adverb means nevertheless, the same sense as for all that.

clue.text: In new arrangement hide plain plants

indicators.note: In new arrangement says the following words have their letters reordered

explanation.surface: Arranging flowers to hide a dull display.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphinia, plural of delphinium, are tall flowering garden plants such as larkspur.

clue.text: Powerful warplane gaining height, latest in technology

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter jet

indicators.note: latest in a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A fighter jet climbing, the newest in military tech.
explanation.definitionFit: Mighty means strong and forceful, a synonym of powerful.

clue.text: Rose maybe is an acceptable model

definitions.meaning: a plant trained onto a single upright stem, often a rose
a benchmark or norm used as a model

explanation.surface: A rose bush could be a decent example to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard names both a tree-form rose and an accepted measure or pattern.
